summary_rationale: Greaves Cotton is two businesses under one roof. The core (engines, gensets, Excel linkages, aftermarket and industrial products) is a real, cash-earning cyclical manufacturer with standalone EBITDA margins of 13-14% for three years and net cash at the core, although the first half of FY27 saw core margins slip to about 12% on commodity costs and one-offs. The consolidated group also carries Greaves Electric Mobility, an electric two-wheeler and L5 three-wheeler maker that is still loss-making, was named in the FAME-II subsidy refund episode, and is funded by parent capital and a rights issue while it works toward break-even. Group cash conversion has been poor: cumulative operating cash flow over FY22-FY26 was negative against positive EBITDA, borrowings (including leases and a captive EV lender's match-funded loans) rose sharply in FY26 and H1 FY27, and first-half FY27 operating cash flow was deeply negative. Volume growth, new customer wins and the improving electric-vehicle unit economics are genuine positives, but the FY30 group revenue ambition is arithmetically stretched against the 16-20% organic plan. Business quality is therefore conditional: sound at the core, unproven at the group level until the EV arm funds itself and working capital normalises.
